summary: Preinstall script downloads Bun runtime and executes obfuscated payload at install time
details: The package declares scripts.preinstall = "node setup.mjs", which fires automatically on npm install. setup.mjs downloads the Bun runtime (bun-v1.3.13) from GitHub, extracts it to a temp directory, chmods the binary executable, and invokes it against sibling file math_init.js via execFileSync(bunPath, ['math_init.js'], {stdio:'inherit'}). math_init.js is a 727 KB single-line JavaScript blob with hex-mangled identifiers (_0xNNNN, MmgoCP, etDiOOB, JqTtnbZ), a large numeric/string constant array, and an array-rotator function (WV8StW pushing/shifting the array) — the canonical obfuscator.io string-array + shuffler pattern. Executing the payload under Bun rather than Node evades tooling that only traces node-resolved code. The package's advertised purpose is React components for mobile webviews, but the declared main (dist/index.js) is a 105-byte re-export of ionicons/icons and there is no substantive library code — the preinstall dropper is the only real functionality. The scope name @servicetitan/anvil2-ext-mwv closely resembles the legitimate @servicetitan/anvil2 scope (also listed as a dependency), author is empty, and README is 0 bytes, consistent with scope impersonation used to deliver the payload.
